source: Open-Meteo archived weather forecasts (Historical Forecast API, Previous Runs API)

license.terms: Free API is for non-commercial use; < 10,000 calls/day, 5,000/hour, 600/minute (https://open-meteo.com/en/terms).

timestamp_convention: Raw JSON 'time' labels are UTC (timezone=GMT). temperature_2m and wind_speed_100m are instantaneous at the label; shortwave_radiation is the mean over the preceding hour. gridpilot.data.weather.load() sets ts_utc = label - 1h (hour-start, like eia930).

coverage_probe.method: 1-day requests: yearly samples (Jan 15, 2015-2025, + 2025-06-01), then bisection by day; a day counts as covered if any hour is non-null

semantics.historical_forecast: Docs: 'Each run's first few hours are stitched into a continuous hourly timeseries.' => each hour comes from a run initialised 0-5 h earlier (0 h for hourly HRRR): near-observed weather, NOT knowable a day ahead. Docs also: 'Not suitable for long time series due to model version changes over time.' best_match in the US switches source: HRRR only (no 100 m wind) until 2021-03-22, HRRR+GFS from 2021-03-23.
semantics.previous_runs: Docs: '_previous_day1 returns the value predicted 24 hours before valid time; _previous_day2 returns 48 hours before'. Launch post: 'the initial 24 hours of each weather model run are disregarded. In models updating every 3 hours, time steps 24, 25, and 26 are utilized' => previous_dayN(t) comes from the latest run initialised <= t - 24N h. Empirical check (PACE_SLC, best_match, 2024): hour-to-hour jumps of temperature_2m_previous_day1 relative to day0 peak at valid 00/06/12 UTC (ratio 1.33/1.23/1.27 vs 0.81-0.95 at adjacent hours) => 6-hourly source runs, lead 24-29 h for day1 and 48-53 h for day2.
semantics.publication_latency: Docs (Single Runs API): 'typically 4-6 hours for global models (e.g. ECMWF IFS, GFS) and 1-3 hours for regional models'. Live meta.json on 2026-10-27: GFS 0.13 5.4 h, HRRR 1.5 h, NBM 0.9 h, ECMWF IFS 0.25 7.6 h, IFS HRES 6.2 h.
semantics.previous_runs_base_equals_historical_for: The un-suffixed Previous Runs variables (day0) equal the Historical Forecast API series exactly (100% of 40,417 overlapping hours, PACE_SLC temperature_2m, 2021-03..2025-10): they leak like HF and must not be used as day-ahead features.

honest_day_ahead_verdict.api: previous-runs (Historical Forecast API leaks: 0-5 h lead)
honest_day_ahead_verdict.rule: previous_dayN at Open-Meteo label t is knowable at issue time I iff t - 24N h <= I - L (L = publication latency). N = ceil((t - I + L) / 24 h): gridpilot.data.weather.safe_previous_day
honest_day_ahead_verdict.issue_10_local_D_minus_1: labels of local day D run to I + 38 h, so N = 2 is honest for every hour of D whenever L <= 10 h (global models: 4-7.6 h). N = 1 is honest only for labels t <= I - L + 24 h, i.e. up to 04:00 local on D with L = 6 h; for later hours it uses runs initialised after the issue time (up to ~14 h after for the last hour).
honest_day_ahead_verdict.recommended: previous_day2 for all hours (simple, honest); optional mixed rule: previous_day1 for the first ~4 local hours of D, previous_day2 after

honest_start.temperature_2m (day1/day2): 2021-03-24 / 2021-03-25, continuous at all 17 P1 points until ts_utc 2023-12-29T22:00Z; then a gap of 492 h (day1) / 516 h (day2) until ts_utc 2024-01-19T10:00Z / 2024-01-20T10:00Z; continuous afterwards (0 nulls 2024-03..2025-10)

honest_day_ahead_verdict.single_runs_api: exact runs by init time exist only from 2026-04-02 (ECMWF HRES from 2024-03-14 as IFS 49r1 hindcasts) => cannot replace Previous Runs for train/validation

findings.rate_limits: Free API: < 10,000 calls/day, 5,000/hour, 600/minute; a request counts max(1, days/14) x max(1, n_vars/10) calls. One full-year Previous Runs request (9 vars) takes ~10-25 s server-side.
